statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is a Vec<bool> with len(r) = len(queries), and for every i with 0 <= i < len(queries), r[i] = true exactly when there is a path between queries[i][0] and queries[i][1] in the undirected graph on cities {1,...,n} where two distinct cities x and y are adjacent iff there exists an integer z such that z > threshold, z divides x, and z divides y. A path is a finite sequence c_0,...,c_k of cities in {1,...,n} with k >= 0, c_0 = queries[i][0], c_k = queries[i][1], and every consecutive pair c_j,c_{j+1} adjacent as just defined.
preconditions: n, threshold, and queries satisfy: 2 <= n <= 10^4; 0 <= threshold <= n; 1 <= len(queries) <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(queries), len(queries[i]) = 2, 1 <= queries[i][0] <= n, 1 <= queries[i][1] <= n, and queries[i][0] != queries[i][1].

statement: For every n, threshold, and queries satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r and does not fail: it does not panic, overflow, go out of bounds, or divide by zero.
preconditions: n, threshold, and queries satisfy: 2 <= n <= 10^4; 0 <= threshold <= n; 1 <= len(queries) <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(queries), len(queries[i]) = 2, 1 <= queries[i][0] <= n, 1 <= queries[i][1] <= n, and queries[i][0] != queries[i][1].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i,j with 0 <= i,j < len(queries), if queries[i][0] = queries[j][1] and queries[i][1] = queries[j][0], then r[i] = r[j].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i,j,k with 0 <= i,j,k < len(queries), if there exist a,b,c such that queries[i] = [a,b], queries[j] = [b,c], queries[k] = [a,c], r[i] = true, and r[j] = true, then r[k] = true.

preconditions: n, threshold, and queries satisfy: 2 <= n <= 10^4; 0 <= threshold <= n; 1 <= len(queries) <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(queries), len(queries[i]) = 2, 1 <= queries[i][0] <= n, 1 <= queries[i][1] <= n, and queries[i][0] != queries[i][1]; additionally threshold = 0.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(queries), if r[i] = true, then there exists an integer k >= 0 and a sequence c_0,...,c_k of integers such that 1 <= c_j <= n for every 0 <= j <= k, c_0 = queries[i][0], c_k = queries[i][1], and for every 0 <= j < k, c_j != c_{j+1} and there exists an integer z > threshold dividing both c_j and c_{j+1}.

statement: If both calls return results r1 and r2, then for every i with 0 <= i < len(Q), if r2[i] = true then r1[i] = true.
preconditions: For all integers n, t1, t2, and all query lists Q such that 2 <= n <= 10^4, 0 <= t1 <= t2 <= n, 1 <= len(Q) <= 10^5, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(Q), len(Q[i]) = 2, 1 <= Q[i][0] <= n, 1 <= Q[i][1] <= n, and Q[i][0] != Q[i][1]. Let r1 be the result of are_connected(n,t1,Q) and r2 be the result of are_connected(n,t2,Q).

statement: If both calls return results r1 and r2, then for every i with 0 <= i < len(Q), if r1[i] = true then r2[i] = true.
preconditions: For all integers n1, n2, t, and all query lists Q such that 2 <= n1 <= n2 <= 10^4, 0 <= t <= n1, 1 <= len(Q) <= 10^5, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(Q), len(Q[i]) = 2, 1 <= Q[i][0] <= n1, 1 <= Q[i][1] <= n1, and Q[i][0] != Q[i][1]. Let r1 be the result of are_connected(n1,t,Q) and r2 be the result of are_connected(n2,t,Q).

statement: If both calls return results r and r', then for every i,j with 0 <= i < len(Q) and 0 <= j < len(Q'), if Q[i][0] = Q'[j][0] and Q[i][1] = Q'[j][1], then r[i] = r'[j].
preconditions: For all integers n, t, and all query lists Q and Q' such that 2 <= n <= 10^4, 0 <= t <= n, both Q and Q' satisfy 1 <= len <= 10^5, every inner vector has length 2, all coordinates are in 1..n, and every pair has distinct endpoints. Let r be the result of are_connected(n,t,Q) and r' be the result of are_connected(n,t,Q').

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(queries), if r[i] = true, then there exists an integer k >= 1 and a sequence c_0,...,c_k of integers such that 1 <= c_j <= n for every 0 <= j <= k, c_0 = queries[i][0], c_k = queries[i][1], the cities c_0,...,c_k are pairwise distinct, and for every 0 <= j < k there exists an integer z > threshold dividing both c_j and c_{j+1}.
preconditions: n, threshold, and queries satisfy: 2 <= n <= 10^4; 0 <= threshold <= n; 1 <= len(queries) <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(queries), len(queries[i]) = 2, 1 <= queries[i][0] <= n, 1 <= queries[i][1] <= n, and queries[i][0] != queries[i][1].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(queries), if (queries[i][0] = threshold+1 and queries[i][1] = 2*(threshold+1)) or (queries[i][0] = 2*(threshold+1) and queries[i][1] = threshold+1), then r[i] = true.
preconditions: n, threshold, and queries satisfy: 2 <= n <= 10^4; 0 <= threshold < floor(n/2); 1 <= len(queries) <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(queries), len(queries[i]) = 2, 1 <= queries[i][0] <= n, 1 <= queries[i][1] <= n, and queries[i][0] != queries[i][1].
